state.question: Assess Harrow Bank's reported bank deposit repricing. I need the following measured result: The average rate actually paid on retail deposits in September versus August, rather than the advertised offer.
state.conclusion: Harrow cut its advertised savings rate after a policy meeting.
state.gap: The average rate actually paid on retail deposits in September versus August, rather than the advertised offer.

candidates.title: Harrow Bank: the weekly notebook
candidates.abstract: Our reporting desk follows Harrow Bank, drawing on an independent correspondent's account of the average rate actually paid on retail deposits in September versus August, rather than the advertised offer.

candidates.title: Harrow Bank: the strategic argument
candidates.abstract: An operating note about Harrow Bank: The advertised instant-access rate was 2.4% at the end of September.

candidates.title: Harrow Bank: the operating record
candidates.abstract: I set out the case for Harrow Bank's strategy in bank deposit repricing, using incentives and managerial judgement to project the next stage.

candidates.title: Harrow Bank: what the announcement changes
candidates.abstract: An edited digest of Arun Patel's Dispatch's dispatch on Harrow Bank, retaining its reported comparison and attribution.

candidates.title: Harrow Bank: the measurement desk
candidates.abstract: A commentary revisiting Harrow Bank's operating announcement, carrying the same factual account as the public record.

candidates.title: Harrow Bank: the latest field dispatch
candidates.abstract: Harrow retail deposit ledger supports a dated assessment of the average rate actually paid on retail deposits in September versus August, rather than the advertised offer.
